repos.title: v0.31.0
repos.body:
HushMessenger v0.31.0 patches Messenger 588.1.0.66.98. It needs Morphe Manager 2.7.0 or newer, or morphe-desktop 2.3.0 on a computer. This release moves to Messenger 588.1.0.66.98, so grab that build from APKMirror and patch it with the same signing key as before. It installs over your current copy and your settings carry over. This one is big. The Instants tab can sit in the bar at the bottom, a chat can play its sound while it's open, and you can pick your own sounds for sending a message. Every chat can show its pinned messages, you can appear offline and still see who's active, and a lot of smaller switches landed under Inbox, Theme and Privacy. `Unlock app icons` and `Unlock app themes` are gone.

### New in this release

- `Show Instants tab` is a new switch under Tab bar, and it starts off. Messenger keeps Instants in its own tab on some accounts and hides it behind a + in Chats on the rest. This puts that tab in the middle of the bar at the bottom. Turn on `Hide the Instants button` too and the + is gone from Chats. Refs #216.
- `Sound in the open chat` is a new switch under Notifications, and it starts off. Messenger stays quiet when a message comes into the chat you have open, unless it's a like or a sticker. With this on you hear its in-app message sound there too, or the one you picked in `Custom chat sounds`. A silent phone and Messenger's own in-app sounds setting still keep it quiet. Refs #224.
- `Custom chat sounds` is a new patch next to `Custom new-message sound`, and it starts unselected. Messenger's double pop when you send a message is really two sounds, one as it goes out and one once it has gone through, and there's a third for a new message while Messenger is open. Pick an .ogg, .mp3, .m4a or .wav file for any of them in Morphe Manager's Expert mode and it plays instead. Refs #224.
- `Show pinned messages` is a new switch under Conversations, and it starts off. Messenger already has a bar under a chat's name that shows its pinned messages, but it only turns that bar on in some chats. With this on every chat gets it. Refs #213.
- `Hide Create story` is a new switch under Inbox, and it starts off. The row of stories and notes above your chats always opens with your own Create story tile, even if you never post one. With this on that tile is gone and the row starts with your friends' stories. Your own story and note sit on that tile, so they go with it. Refs #225.
- `Hide Suggested in search` and `Hide recent reels in search` are new switches under Inbox, and both start off. Tap the search bar and, before you type a thing, Messenger fills the screen with people it suggests and the reels you watched lately. Turn these on and those sections are gone, so search opens empty and waits for you. Anyone you search for by name still comes up. Refs #207.
- `Jump to the first message or a date` has a `Page up and page down buttons` switch under it now, and it starts off. Reading back through a long chat meant swiping over and over. With this on, two buttons sit over the jump arrow at the bottom left of a chat, and each tap moves the chat most of a screen up or down, so the last lines you read stay in view. Each one only shows while there's more to see that way. Refs #207.
- `Hide Meta AI` reaches into search now. Meta AI's own sections are gone from search, and so are Meta AI and the other AI bots when you type their name, which used to be the way back into a chat with one. Refs #204.
- `Block Meta AI chats` is a new switch under Navigation, and it starts off. Hiding Meta AI took its buttons away, but a chat with it could still open from a link someone sent you or an old chat in your list. With this on, a chat with Meta AI or another AI bot doesn't open at all, and a short message says why. A group chat with an AI in it still opens, since there are people in there too. Refs #204.
- `Thin story rings` is a new switch under Theme, and it starts off. The colored ring around someone's picture when they have a story is thick enough to crowd a small picture. With this on it's drawn at half the width in the same spot, and square profile pictures get the thinner ring too. Refs #215.
- The Material You theme takes color codes now. Under the accent swatches there's a field for the accent and one for the background. Type codes like #E1306C, tap `Use these colors`, and Material You uses them in dark and light mode. Leave one empty and Messenger keeps its own color there. Refs #211.
- Material You themes save to a file now. `Save theme to a file` writes the theme in use as a small .json file wherever you pick, named after the theme, and `Open a theme file` brings one back with Undo, the same as `Use copied theme`. So a theme you made can live in your Downloads or go to a friend without the clipboard. Refs #115.
- `Screen refresh rate` is a new switch under Theme, and it starts off. Android decides how fast Messenger's screen refreshes, and plenty of phones keep apps at 60 Hz or run them at full speed no matter what you'd rather have. Turn it on and pick a rate from the ones your screen does, slower to save battery or faster for smoother scrolling. Your phone can still say no, in power saving mode for one. Refs #208.
- `Write longer notes` is a new switch under Inbox, and it starts off. The note box takes up to 500 characters instead of 60, and Facebook still decides whether a long note goes through. Refs #199.
- `Show the 40-character code option` is a new switch under Privacy, and it starts off. Some accounts see `More options` in Message storage where `Generate 40-character code` used to be. With this on you get both rows, and the code row opens Messenger's own setup. Refs #197.
- `Chat bar buttons in the + menu` is a new switch under Conversations, and it starts off. The camera, gallery and mic sit in a row beside the message box and leave it very little room. With this on, only + stays there. Those buttons move into the menu + opens, and tapping one does what it always did. Needs Android 10 or newer. Refs #198.
- `Hide profile menu items` is a new switch under Chat menu, and it starts off. Tapping someone's picture beside their message opens a menu with View profile, the call options and more. Tap one picture once and those items show up under the switch, where you can hide the ones you never use. The menu always keeps at least one. `Ask before a call` now asks on that menu's Audio call and Video call too. Refs #201.
- `Hide messages with your words` is a new switch under Privacy, and it starts off. There are words you'd rather not have appear on your screen, whether it's a name, a spoiler or something that just ruins your afternoon, and Messenger gives you nothing for that short of muting the whole chat. Type the words under the switch, separated by commas, and a message that comes in with one of them shows as "[hidden]" in the chat and puts up no notification at all. A whole word has to match, so "ok" doesn't hide "okay", and capital letters make no difference. Encrypted chats are covered the same way. Nothing goes back to the sender and nothing is deleted, so the message is still there on their phone, and the messages you send go out as they always did. The chat list's last line still shows Messenger's own preview of the message. Refs #196.
- `Swipe between tabs` is a new switch under Tab bar, and it starts off. Messenger's home screen swaps one tab's page for another instead of sliding between them, so the only way to the next tab is reaching down to its button, and on a tall phone that means moving your whole hand. With this on, a sideways swipe across your chats moves you one tab along the bar, and a swipe the other way brings you back. Tabs you've hidden are skipped, so the swipe follows what the bar is actually showing you. Anything inside a tab that scrolls sideways on its own keeps its own gesture, and a swipe too short to count just lets go. Restart Messenger after you turn it on. Refs #194.
- `Typing in your chat list` is a new switch under Inbox, and it starts off. Messenger only tells you someone is typing once you're already in the chat, so from the list you can't tell who's about to say something. It turns out Messenger has the whole thing built already. The chat list knows how to subscribe for typing and keep track of who's at it, and there's a piece that writes the word over a chat's last message, where the preview normally sits. Meta's server just answers no every time Messenger asks whether any of it should run. With this on, the answer is yes, and a chat in your list says typing while the other person types, then goes back to its last message. Nothing is sent about you, and your own `Hide typing indicator` switch is untouched. Restart Messenger after you turn it on. Refs #195.
- `Put your words above the photo` is a new switch under Photos and videos, and it starts off. Type something, attach a photo or a video, and Messenger hangs what you typed off the bottom of the picture as a caption, where a longer line gets cut short and the picture is all anyone sees at a glance. With this on, your words leave first as a message of their own and the photo lands under them. Names you tagged go with the words. Type nothing and nothing changes: the photo goes out by itself, the way it always did. Refs #195.
- Notifications have their own section in settings and in Morphe's patch list now. `Quiet mode` is in it, and `Notify for restricted chats` has moved there out of Privacy, since what it changes is whether a chat notifies you. Refs #190.
- `Quiet mode` is a new switch under Notifications, and it starts off. Taking a break from Messenger used to mean turning its notifications off in Android settings and then remembering to turn them back on. With this on, HushMessenger settings gets a break button: 15 minutes, an hour, two hours, eight hours, or until you end it yourself. For that long nothing from Messenger makes a sound or buzzes your phone. Messages and calls still arrive and still wait in the notification shade, so nothing goes missing while you're away from it. There's an `Every night` switch under it as well, with a start and an end time, for the hours you'd rather not hear from anybody. Anyone on your `Special contacts` list comes through as usual, whether they message you or call. Refs #190.
- `Invisible buttons` is a new switch under Theme, and it starts off. Messenger is full of buttons you may never use, and a couple of them sit right where your thumb lands. Hiding one outright isn't the answer, because the gap it leaves still reacts to a tap, which is how people end up in a video call they didn't want. With this on, you pick buttons in HushMessenger settings and set each one to invisible, or to a quarter, half or three quarters of how Messenger draws it. The button keeps its place, its size, the area that answers a tap and whatever it did before, so nothing shuffles around and a deliberate tap still works. It reaches anywhere in Messenger, from the chat list to the menu a long press brings up, and buttons HushMessenger adds count too. The list fills itself as Messenger shows you buttons, each one named the way a screen reader says it, so use Messenger for a bit before you go looking. Refs #191.
- `Translucent chat bars` is a new switch under Theme, and it starts off. Messenger's chat has a solid bar across the top and a solid box at the bottom, and the messages stop dead at both of them. With this on, the messages are given that room and scroll under the bars, and each bar draws what's behind it blurred, so the thread shows through the way it does on an iPhone. The bar's own color goes over the blur, so dark mode and any theme you picked still look like themselves. The banner at the top of a chat and the button back to the newest message stay where they were. Needs Android 12 or newer, and a chat that was already open needs opening again. Refs #162.
- `Play video links in the chat` is a new switch under Links and bubbles, and it starts off. Someone sends you a YouTube, TikTok, Instagram or Facebook video and tapping it throws you out of the conversation: either into Messenger's own browser or into another app you then have to come back from. With this on, the video opens in a window over the chat instead. Play, pause and play again sit on the video for YouTube links, there's a full screen button in the corner, and the name of the site in the other corner opens the link where it would have gone. The video comes from the site's own player, the window gets a cookie jar of its own that's emptied when it opens and again when it closes, and nothing is saved to your phone. Shortened links (youtu.be aside), Facebook stories and anything that isn't a video page open the way they always did. Refs #188.
- `Blur behind menus` has a `Floating message menu` switch under it now. Press and hold a message and Messenger drops Reply, Copy, Delete and the rest into a bar across the very bottom of the screen, which is a stretch on a tall phone. With this on, those same actions come up as a rounded card right under the message you pressed, the way an iPhone does it, and the bar at the bottom goes away. When the message is the last one on the screen, it moves up with its emoji row so the card fits under it (with `Blur behind menus` off, the card goes above the emoji row there instead). Swipe to reply is untouched. Every row on the card is Messenger's own action, so Reply, Edit, Unsend, Forward, Copy and More still do exactly what they did. Refs #176.
- Messenger's Menu tab has a `Menu tab` section in HushMessenger's App settings now, listing every row Messenger puts there: Communities, Channel invites, Marketplace, whatever your account gets. Hide the ones you never open and the Menu tab comes back short. Each row turns up in settings once the Menu tab has shown it, so open it once after you patch, and the last row standing can't be hidden. There's a `Log out row in the Menu tab` switch in the same section as well, which puts Log out right under Settings and signs you out the way Messenger's own Log out does. Refs #189.
- `Block screenshots in chats` is a new switch under Privacy. With it on, Android refuses a screenshot or a screen recording while a chat is open, and the chat doesn't show up in the app switcher's preview either. It covers every chat, not just the ones with disappearing messages on, and a chat that was already open needs opening again. It only guards this phone, so the person you're chatting with can still screenshot on theirs. Refs #187.
- View-once photos and Quicksnap get a Save button of their own. `Allow screenshots` already let the phone's screenshot through, but a view-once photo tends to close or get unsent while you're still reaching for the buttons, and the swipe gesture shuts the viewer instead of catching it. Turn on `Save button on view-once media` under the same switch and the viewer gets a Save pill in the corner: one tap puts what's on screen into Pictures/Messenger, and the pill keeps itself out of the picture. On a video it saves the frame you're looking at. Needs Android 10 or newer. Refs #181, #5.
- `Offer View once in every chat` is a new switch under Photos and videos, and it starts off. Open the gallery in a chat and the View once toggle is there for some people and missing for others, because Messenger asks a server which chats are allowed it, and a group chat never is. With this on, the gallery offers the toggle wherever it opens, group chats included. The switch can only add the toggle, never take it away, so every chat that already had it keeps it. What the Messenger on the other end does with a photo sent that way is Meta's call, not this switch's, so treat a photo you'd hate to see saved the way you would anywhere else. Refs #192.
- `Hide tab labels` is a new switch under Navigation. The words under the icons at the bottom of the screen say what every Messenger user already knows, and on a small phone they crowd the bar. With this on the labels go and the icons stay, roomier and a little quieter to look at. TalkBack still reads out the name of every tab, so nothing is lost if you use a screen reader. Restart Messenger after you turn it on. Refs #186.
- `Your own tab icons` is a new switch under Tab bar. Messenger's bottom icons are its own filled shapes and there's never been a way to change them. Turn this on and every tab gets a plain outlined icon instead, drawn in the same color Messenger was using, so the selected tab still looks selected and dark mode still looks right. Under the switch there's a row for each tab with a Choose button: pick a picture from your phone and that tab wears it. Remove puts the plain icon back. Pictures stay on this phone and get shrunk to tab size when you pick them. Restart Messenger after you change anything here. Refs #186.
- `Show settings tab` is a new switch under Navigation. Messenger has a settings tab of its own, the round one with your picture on it that sits at the end of the bottom bar, but it only builds it for some accounts. This puts it there on any account, so your Messenger settings are one tap away instead of a trip through the inbox. Restart Messenger after you turn it on. Refs #184.
- The settings screen is in Spanish now. Refs #183.
- `Paste a photo into the chat` is a new switch under Photos and videos. Paste a photo into a chat and Messenger sends it right then: no preview, no caption, no HD, and nothing to cancel. With this on, the photo lands above the message box the way a pick from your gallery does and waits for you to tap Send. Pasted text and the keyboard's GIFs work as they did, and a chat that's already open needs reopening once after you turn it on. Refs #180.
- `Hide read receipts` has a `Hide Delivered` switch under it now. Hiding Seen only ever covered the second tick. The first one, the Delivered tick that appears the moment your phone picks a message up, still went out and told the other person their message had landed on your phone. With this on, that goes no further: your phone takes the message as it always did, and nothing is sent back to say so. It covers ordinary chats. Encrypted chats send Delivered on a path of their own and still show it, and turning `Hide read receipts` off turns this off with it. Refs #61.
- `Mark chats read on this phone` is a new switch under Privacy, for when you're using `Hide read receipts`. Holding the receipt back also meant Messenger never marked the chat read for you, so a chat you'd opened and read through stayed bold in the list with a count sitting next to it. With this on, that unread look clears the moment you open the chat. Nothing goes out to Messenger, so the other person still isn't told you read it, and a new message brings the bold and the count back. Refs #178.
- `Stop attention time logging` is a new switch under Tracking, and it starts off. Every time you leave a screen, Messenger files a report on what held your attention while you were there. It has a timestamp for every thing that came on screen and every one that left, so it says how long you looked at each one and in what order, and it counts the times you came back for another look. With this on, that report isn't filed, and neither is the copy of those timings that goes onto Messenger's journey log. The session's own bookkeeping runs as it always did, so nothing else changes. Refs #80.
- `Appear offline` is a new switch under Privacy, and it starts off. Messenger has only ever offered one answer here: turn Active status off and nobody sees you, but you stop seeing anybody either, dots gone from the chat list and the People tab. As far as Messenger is concerned those are the same setting. With this on they come apart. Leave Active status on where it is, and Messenger keeps telling you who's around while it stops telling anyone about you, whether you're in a chat, in the app or off doing something else. It takes hold the next time Messenger goes to the background or comes back, so restarting it makes the change land right away, and turning the switch off puts you back where you were. Refs #135, #50, #171.
- `Keep a message log` has a `Keep photos at full size` switch under it now, and it starts off. A photo that's unsent before you open it used to leave the log with a thumbnail at best, because the only copy on your phone was the little preview Messenger put on the notification, and an end-to-end encrypted chat doesn't even send that. With this on, the photo itself is downloaded the moment the message is logged, at the size it was sent, from the address the message arrived with. Encrypted chats included. It's kept under the log's own encryption and the log's screen shows it as big as your screen allows. Photos take a lot more room than text, which is why the switch starts off, and each one goes when its message does. Refs #175.
- `Keep a message log` has a `Keep videos` switch under it now, and it starts off. A video is the same story as a photo: Messenger leaves it on its servers until you open it, so one that's unsent before then is gone, and the log's entry has nothing but the line the notification showed. With this on, the video is downloaded as the message is logged and sealed with the rest of the log. A video arrives with its thumbnail's address beside its own and nothing to say which is which, so the log asks for the size of each and keeps the big one. The log's entry gets a Play video button that plays it in a window over the log, straight from the log's own copy, so nothing is written out in the clear. Videos are the biggest thing the log keeps, up to 16 MB each, which is why the switch starts off, and each one goes when its message does. Refs #175.
- `Keep a message log` has a `Keep voice messages` switch under it now, and it starts off. A voice message that's unsent before you play it leaves nothing behind. The log has the message, but the clip was never on your phone, because Messenger waits for you to tap play before it downloads one. With this on, the clip is fetched the moment the message is logged, from the same address the message arrived with, and kept with the log's pictures under the same encryption. The log's entry gets a Play button, so you can hear it there whether or not it's still in the chat. Clips take a lot more room than the rest of the log, which is why the switch starts off, and each one goes when its message does. Refs #175.
- `Skip passkey sign-in` is a new switch under Privacy, and it starts off. Some logins get past the password and then send you round the browser check again and again with no way through. It's accounts that have a passkey: the passkey check wants the Messenger Meta signed, a patched one can't be that, and the login never finishes. The way out so far was to sign in on a computer and delete the passkey first. With this on, the credential providers Messenger asks about passkeys answer that there's nothing here to ask, which is what a phone with no passkey support answers, and Facebook falls back to approving the login from another device you're signed in on. Messenger can't use a passkey for its encrypted backups while it's on either, so turn it back off once you're in. A long press on Messenger's home screen icon opens HushMessenger settings without signing in, which is where you'll be when you need this. Refs #108.

### Fixes and changes

- Remove the `Unlock app icons` patch.
- Remove the `Unlock app themes` patch.
- `Use system emoji` sits under Theme now and `Android Auto messages` under Notifications, in the settings and in Morphe's patch list. Conversations had grown long enough to need scrolling, and those two were always more about how Messenger looks and where your messages get read out than about the chat itself.
- The message log looks like Messenger's own chats now. It used to open on the settings page's pure black with boxed cards. Now it has Messenger's softer greys, or white in light mode, grey message bubbles, a rounded search field and a chat list with each chat's newest message under its name. Every chat gets a round picture, taken from the ones chat notifications already carry, locked with the log's key and cleared along with the chat. It follows Material You and the pure black switch when you have those on. Refs #200.
- Reacting to a message sends the Seen that `Hide read receipts` held back for that chat, the way replying already did. Messenger only lets you react from inside the chat, so a reaction with no Seen looked odd to the sender, and you had to tap `Mark as read` after every one. Refs #223.
- Each section heading in settings counts its switches that are on, like Inbox 3/11, and the count follows your taps. During a search it counts what the search found. Refs #207.
- Searching settings for "reset" offers a `Reset settings` link now. It takes you to `Back to defaults` in Quick setups, which turns every switch off in one tap, and Undo brings them back. Refs #207.
- A chat opened as an Android bubble draws its videos the way Messenger does again. The chat head video fix in 0.30.0 also swapped how videos draw inside bubbles, and on some phones that left a black box over a link's preview and blanked the bubble when you tapped the gallery button. Bubbles never had the chat head problem, so they're back to Messenger's own way. Chat heads keep the fix. Refs #221.
- The story eye (`Mark as seen button`) marks the story you're looking at again. Messenger loads the next story in the background while you watch one, and the eye used to go with whichever story loaded last, so a tap marked the next story as seen and left the one on screen unseen. It follows the story on screen as you swipe now. Refs #202.
- `Auto reply` answers Marketplace chats now. Messenger files a Marketplace conversation under a chat type of its own instead of the one-to-one type, so auto reply took every buyer and seller for a group and stayed quiet unless `Answer in group chats too` was on. The message log's Direct filter shows those chats now too, since there's only ever one other person in them. Refs #227.
- The patches now take Messenger 588.1.0.66.98 and drop 587. All 20 of 588's builds on APKMirror are covered, the four armv7 ones included. Refs #145.
- `Stop attention time logging` has one report left to stop on 588. Messenger no longer copies those timings onto its journey log, so the switch's description doesn't mention that copy anymore. Refs #145.
- TalkBack stops treating the help lines and dividers in `Quick setups` as buttons. Each one was set up to catch a press and hold, so a screen reader stopped on every line and on unnamed, one pixel tall dividers. A press and hold anywhere on the section still hides it.
- `Report a problem` and `Copy setup` say which patches your Messenger was built from now, on a new Bundle line. Someone else published patches under the same name and version number as an official release, and from the version alone I couldn't tell their build from mine. Only the official bundle is signed with this project's key, so the line reads "official, signed" for it and "unsigned" or "signed with another key" for anything else.
- A choices backup brings back more than your switches now. It used to carry only the on and off of each switch, so a new phone or a fresh install got Auto reply turned on with no replies to send, and your hidden chats, local pins, header text and the other lists you'd set up were gone. A backup now holds your auto replies, hidden and pinned chats, the words you hide, your home header, how long the message log keeps messages, your quiet hours, call recording and caption choices, your theme and font sizes, and the rows you hid from menus. Each one goes through the same limits its own row uses, so a hand-edited backup can't save anything the row wouldn't. A backup with replies in it can turn Auto reply on, since it brings the replies along. Older backups still restore their switches like before. A backup is capped at 128 KB. When your choices don't fit, nothing is copied or saved, and the line under the buttons names the setting that's taking up the room. After a restore the page opens again so the restored lists show, and the result stays under the buttons. Refs #152.
- `Save choices to a file` brings your pictures and your font along now. Some choices live in files of their own: the home header picture, the tab pictures, a font you added, the pictures your auto replies send and the people `Special contacts` follows. A restore on a new phone used to turn those switches on with nothing behind them. When you have any of them, Save writes a .zip that carries them next to your choices, and Restore reads either kind, so your older .txt backups still work. Each file goes back through the same checks a pick from that row gets. One that fails them is skipped and counted under the buttons, and the rest still come back. Special contacts come back as who you follow, without what was seen of them. The clipboard backup stays text only. Refs #152.
- `Log chats that don't notify` now covers end-to-end encrypted chats, which is most one-to-one chats these days. A muted encrypted chat's message never reached the log, because Messenger decides that one in its own native code and files the message as already seen before anything in the app gets a look at it. With the switch on, that decision is left to the app, so the message goes to the log and the notification is dropped the same way it already was in an ordinary chat. Messenger reads that code as it starts, so there's a restart button on the switch. Turning it off puts Messenger's own check straight back. Android 17 won't load that code while anything can write to it, so the change goes into a fresh read-only copy that takes the old one's place in one step, and Messenger's own file is never left open for writing, not even for a moment. Refs #143.
- A copy of Messenger renamed by a patch other than `Clone install under another package name` opens now instead of stopping on its loading screen. Messenger looks up its backup settings by its own package name and throws when that name isn't its own, which is where the copy died. The new `Keep a renamed copy working` patch keeps that one lookup on Messenger's name, and sends attachments, muted chats and hidden friendships to the copy's own storage rather than to the Messenger it was copied from. It's always on, with nothing to switch, and the copies `Clone install` makes are untouched. Refs #185.
- `Source and licenses` on the App tab shows the license notices right there in settings now, with no connection needed, where it used to send you off to GitHub. That's the project's NOTICE file in full, and it now carries Morphe's own notice word for word as Morphe asks. A `Source code` button at the bottom still opens the project page. The credits line under it names Morphe too, in every language settings come in.
- `Keep unsent messages` lets go of its oldest unsent messages first once it's holding as many as it keeps (4,096). It used to drop whichever ones came up first, so a message unsent yesterday could lose its words while one from months back kept them.
- `Hide growth prompts` now also hides the "Turn on active status" line Messenger puts under someone's name at the top of a chat while your own active status is off. With the switch off, the line shows as before. Refs #195.
- Privacy was getting long to scroll, so the seven `Stop ...` switches have a `Tracking` section of their own now. Same switches under the same names, and nothing you'd already turned on needs turning on again.
- The patches are built with Morphe patcher 2.5.0 now, the one that comes with Morphe Manager 2.7.0 and Morphe Desktop 2.3.0. Manager won't load a bundle made with a newer patcher than its own, so update Manager to 2.7.0 or newer (or Desktop to 2.3.0) before you add this release.
- The questions HushMessenger asks inside a chat look like the rest of the app now. `Ask before a call` and `Jump to the first message or a date` used to put up Android's flat grey box with its shouting buttons, right on top of your chat. They come up as a rounded card in the chat's own colour instead, with Call filled in and Cancel plain next to it. The card is frosted glass, so your chat shows through it softly blurred with a light edge around it. That works on phones whose Android won't blur behind a window as well, since the card blurs its own copy of the chat. Refs #179.
- `Ask before a call` asks in a chat head too. A chat head draws in a window Messenger puts over other apps, with no screen behind it for a dialog to sit on, so the question went up as nothing and the call started anyway. `Jump to a date` was blind in the same spot, and its menu and date picker now open in a chat head as well. Refs #172.
- `Keep unsent messages` keeps the words of an unsent message after you close Messenger from the multitasking screen. In an encrypted chat those words were only held in memory, so the "deleted a message" row came back blank once the app had been swiped away. They're now written to a small sealed file of their own, which means clearing the message log doesn't take them, and only messages you've already seen unsent are written there. An unsend that happens while Messenger isn't running still arrives with nothing to show. Refs #70, #172.
- The Record button on a call sits at the bottom now, above Messenger's own call buttons, and it's a little smaller. It used to sit in the top bar, right over the name of the person you were calling as the call started. Refs #105.
- `Record calls` can keep the two sides of a call apart. A recording has always been both voices added together, which is fine for listening back and no help at all when you're trying to make out what one person said over the top of the other. `The two sides` under the switch has an option that puts you on the left channel and them on the right, so either voice can be pulled out or simply listened to on its own. The file is twice the size, and both ways play in anything. Together is still what you get unless you change it. Refs #193.
- A saved call recording can go straight into a chat, which is the easy way to keep one somewhere you'll find it again. The notification `Notify when a call is saved` puts up has a `Send in a chat` button next to Share: it opens Messenger's own chat picker with the recording attached, so sending it to yourself is two taps and the file is then in your history on every phone you sign in on. `Share` still hands it to anything else on the phone. The notification also offers the recording as the type it was actually saved as, so an Opus one goes out as an .ogg rather than claiming to be a WAV. Refs #193.
- `Record calls` can start a recording for you. `Calls to record` sits at the top of the control: leave it on `Only when I tap Record` and nothing changes, pick `Every call` and the recording starts the moment a call connects, or pick `Only chosen chats` and switch on the people you want. That list fills itself from the chats that have called you, and a call you place is matched by the name on the call screen. The button still says Stop, so you can end any recording early, and once you do it stays ended for that call. Refs #193.
- `Record calls` can save a call as Opus instead of a WAV. An hour of call runs to around 115 MB as a WAV, which fills a phone fast if you record often. `Save calls as` under the switch offers OGG Opus instead, where the same hour is nearer 10 MB and the voices sound much the same. WAV is still what you get unless you change it, since it plays in anything. Your phone's own encoder does the work, and a phone that hasn't got one says so in settings and keeps saving WAVs. Refs #193.
- `Record calls` can put your recordings wherever you want them. They've always gone to the phone's own Recordings folder, which is no help if that's the drive filling up or you'd rather they landed somewhere that syncs. `Recordings folder` under the switch has a Pick a folder button: choose any folder Android lets you write to, an SD card or a cloud app's folder included, and calls are written straight there with no copying afterwards. Use the default puts it back. The folder is remembered across restarts, the tidy-up under `Keep recordings` works there the same way, and a folder that's been moved or taken away since you picked it falls back to the phone's own rather than losing the call. Refs #193.
- `Record calls` has two more rows of its own under it now. `Keep recordings` takes the old ones away for you: leave it on Keep them all, or pick a week, a month or three months, and anything past that goes after the next call is saved. Only the recordings this made are counted, so a file you moved or renamed yourself is left alone, and so is everything else in the folder. `Notify when a call is saved` puts the finished recording in your notifications with its file name, where a tap plays it and Share sends it on. Both start off. Refs #193.
- `Record calls` names a recording after whoever the call was with, counts the time on the button while it runs, and has a Pause next to it. A file called "Call 2026-11-17 14.02.11" told you nothing about which call it was, so the name now reads "Call with Alex Kim" and the date after it. The button itself says Stop 1:12 as the recording goes, and Pause holds it: the part you skip is left out of the file rather than saved as silence, and Resume picks it back up. A call with nobody's name on screen is still saved under the plain date. Refs #193.
- Videos stop leaving a black box behind on Huawei and Honor phones. Messenger draws a video on a layer of its own, and on those phones the layer stayed on screen after the video had gone, in the chat as well as in a chat head. Videos there are now drawn in the chat itself, the way chat head videos already were. Every other phone is left as it was. Refs #104.
- `Jump to the first message or a date` now takes a tap on one of the dates between a chat's messages. The day picker opens on the day you tapped, so getting back to a day you can see on screen is one tap and a Jump instead of a long press and a scroll through the calendar. Nothing in Messenger answers a tap there, so no chat loses anything, and a tap on a message is still Messenger's. Refs #177.
- `Jump to the first message or a date` also puts a round arrow at the bottom left of a chat. Tap it to go to the chat's first message, press and hold it to pick a day. The long press on the chat's name still does the same thing, it was just hard to come across. The arrow shows up once you've scrolled up a little and there's more to go to, it steps aside while a jump is counting or a message's menu is open, and it rides above the keyboard like the count bar does. Refs #177.
- `Auto reply` answers as soon as it can instead of a second and a half later. The reply goes out through the chat's notification, which Messenger posts a moment after the message lands, so the answer used to sit out a fixed wait long enough to cover the slowest phone. It now looks for that notification almost at once and keeps looking on a short beat until it's there. Refs #182.
- `Live captions on calls` lets you pick a language your phone didn't list. Both language sheets only showed what the phone's own speech and translation services report they can do, and that report leaves out languages they handle fine once asked. Filipino is one of them, which is what your phone calls Tagalog. Each sheet ends in `Another language…` now, and that one opens every language the phone knows about. Pick what the other side speaks and the phone fetches that model first. Refs #159.
- `Blur behind menus` now covers the menu you get when you press and hold a message, too. Messenger draws that menu inside the chat rather than in a window of its own, so the switch never saw it. Now the chat behind it blurs under a light shade and the message you pressed stays sharp on top of it. Needs Android 12 or newer. Refs #162.
- Morphe Manager now treats a copy made with `Clone install under another package name` as a clone, so its card gets the Clone chip and stays apart from your regular Messenger. If you changed the copy's package name in that patch's options, type it in again before you repatch, because Manager won't carry the old one over. The app name you picked stays.
- `Stop app list and device ID sharing` no longer stops patching when Morphe's `Spoof signature` is picked too. That patch reroutes Messenger's installed-app list through its own code before ours runs, so the switch didn't recognize the list anymore and threw "the device ID sync changed". The switch now finds the list either way. The Facebook clone option had the same blind spot with its "is Facebook installed" check and now follows the clone either way too. Refs #174.

### Reports this release changed something for

hushfeed.title: v0.85.0
hushfeed.body:
Hushfeed v0.85.0 has 156 patches for global TikTok 47.9.3 (`com.zhiliaoapp.musically`), and 15 of them also work on TikTok Lite 47.8.2 (`com.zhiliaoapp.musically.go`). It needs Morphe Manager 2.7.0 or newer, or morphe-desktop 2.3.0 on a computer.

TikTok stays on 47.9.3, so patch the same build with the same signing key and your login and settings carry over. A favorite that gets deleted now keeps its cover and creator with `Remember saved videos`, and `Keep your place in chats` stops a chat you scrolled up in from jumping to the bottom. TikTok Lite picks up SIM spoof, Ghost mode, the publish date and the author's region. The Feature Gate Lab no longer lists or changes gates tied to what TikTok sells.

New in this release

- `Remember saved videos` is new in Feed screen, next to the Favorites grid options. As your Favorites load, Hushfeed keeps each video's cover, creator, caption and post date on your phone. When TikTok later marks a saved video as deleted or unplayable, its grey tile shows the kept cover and creator instead, and a tap shows the rest. `Unavailable saved videos` lists them all with a search box. It can only keep what it saw while a video was still up, so tiles that were already grey stay grey (#516).
- `Fill wide videos too`, right under `Fill the screen with the video`, crops landscape and square videos to cover the screen as well. Fill on its own still leaves those whole, so you see all of a landscape video with bars above and below it. Turn this on and every video fills the screen, showing the middle of a wide one (#505).
- `Keep your place in chats` stops a chat you've scrolled up in from jumping to the bottom on its own. Coming back from a video you opened in the chat leaves you where you were, and so does sending a reply to an older message. A plain message you send and the down arrow still take you to the newest. It starts off and sits under `Show message times` in Hushfeed settings > Inbox (#503).
- On the floating bottom bar, `Glass lens on the current tab` is the same thin outline as on TikTok's own bar now, with nothing filled inside, so the video shows through it like it does around it. The glass and see-through bars keep the glass bubble (#483).
- When the diagnostic report says the phone destroyed TikTok's main screen, it now says why it might have. Either Don't keep activities is on in Developer options, or it gives how full TikTok's memory was, since Android closes an app's screens in the background once three quarters of it is used (#419).
- `Show how long a LIVE has been on`, with the other LIVE options in Playback, adds how long the host has been live to the small line in LIVE rooms, counted from when the room started and ticking every second. It sits under the room ID when that's on too. A room opened from the LIVE feed shows it once TikTok has that room's start time. It starts off (#494).
- `Show exact LIVE battle scores` shows a battle's whole score where TikTok caps it for viewers at 1M+ (or at the server's own limit with a + after it) and only the host sees the number. It covers the battle bar, the co-host windows and the high score notice. The supporters list is a page TikTok's server draws, so it isn't covered. It starts off (#495).
- `Start LIVEs at` is new under `Offer LIVE quality in more rooms`. Pick a quality there and every LIVE room opens at it until you pick another one in a room, and that pick then carries to the next rooms until TikTok closes. A room whose stream doesn't have the quality opens at TikTok's choice. It starts at `The quality you picked last`, which is how rooms opened before (#57).
- `Skip promo lines` is new under Feed filter, with its own `Promo words` list. When a line of a video's captions has one of your words, like casino or promo code, the video jumps past it and shows Undo, which goes back and lets that part play. It reads the video's own captions, so a video without any plays as usual. It's part of Subtitle tools and starts off (#493).
- `Show the country and date under the caption` has three settings of its own under Feed screen now: a text size (0 keeps the post date's size, or pick 8 to 48 points), an opacity from 10 to 100, and a shadow under the letters for bright videos (#500).
- `Tap brings the controls back` is new under `Automatic Clear display`. A tap on a video whose controls it hid shows them again instead of pausing the video, and they hide again after the delay, or after 3 seconds if the delay is shorter (#501).
- `Burn-in guard dim level` sets how solid the buttons, caption and tabs stay while the burn-in guard has them dimmed, from 0 to 90. It used to be fixed at 25. At 0 they're gone until your next touch (#501).
- `Hold speed bubble size` is new under `Slide to change the hold speed`. It draws the bubble from 50 to 150 percent of its usual size. Since 0.82.0 the bubble grows with your phone's font size, which made it big with large text on, so set it under 100 to bring it back down (#452).
- `Fade the controls out` is new under `Automatic Clear display`. The buttons, caption and tabs fade away over a quarter second before the clear instead of vanishing at once, and a touch during the fade brings them back. It starts off (#501).
- `Date instead of age` is new next to the publish date options. Recent videos show the day they were posted, like 10-12 or Oct 12, where TikTok writes 2d ago, and today's and yesterday's videos get a date too. `Day before month` and `Write the month as a word` change it the same way. It starts off (#461).
- `SIM spoof`, `Ghost mode`, `Always show publish date` and `Show author region` work on TikTok Lite now. SIM spoof uses the same Region settings as in TikTok. Lite's Ghost mode has `Hide story views`, `Hide profile visits`, `Hide typing` and `Hide online status`. The publish date shows next to the creator's name on every Lite video, For You included, and the date options change it there too. With `Show where a video was posted` on, the country comes after the date, or stands alone where Lite leaves the date off. Lite's video data does carry it, but Lite throws it away while it reads the feed, so Hushfeed picks it up there (#502).
- `Random time each day` is new under `Keep a streak going`. The message goes out at a different time every day, somewhere between `When to send` and `Latest time`, so friends don't get it at the same minute each day. It starts off (#507).
- `Jump to a date on Favorites grids` does for your saved videos what the Liked one does for likes. A button in the Favorites grid's top corner starts the list at the year or month you pick, so old saves load without scrolling through thousands of newer ones, and Newest saves goes back. It starts off and sits under `Jump to a date on Liked grids` in Hushfeed settings > Feed screen (#508).
- `Pick a built-in font` is new under `Import a font file` on the App page. It lists 26 fonts that come with Hushfeed, like Bebas Neue, Lobster, Press Start 2P and VT323, and each name in the list is drawn in its own font. The one you pick becomes your imported font, so turn on `Use an imported font` and restart TikTok to see it (#487).
- `Delete your picked posts` is new under `Pick videos to save from profile grids` in Downloads. While every post you've picked on a grid is your own, the picking bar gets a trash button. It counts down from 5 with Stop, then deletes the posts from your account one at a time with a short pause between them, and each one leaves the grid as it goes. A deleted post can't be brought back, so it starts off (#487).
- `Account facts on profiles` shows how many posts an account has. Liked videos, favorites and reposts get a line of their own on the profiles TikTok sends those numbers for, and many profiles come without them. A number TikTok left out or sent as 0 gets no line, since the two look the same (#487).
- The settings screen now comes in Bulgarian, shown when TikTok runs in Bulgarian or when you pick it under `Hushfeed language`. It's a first pass, so corrections from Bulgarian speakers are welcome (#517).
- `Export followers and following` can save a JSON or plain text file as well as CSV. Tapping it lists each choice, like `Followers (JSON)` or `Following (Plain text)`. The JSON file has the same details as the CSV, and the plain text one is a username on each line (#487).
- TikTok Lite's settings no longer list switches that did nothing there. Lite's feed filter works on the videos in the feed and nothing else, so its Feed filter page drops `Hide TikTok Shop in search`, the search tab list, `Show only mutual friends on the Friends tab`, `Latest first on Following`, both offline video switches and `Show how many were filtered`. Its Feed screen page drops `Hide the search bar below videos`, `Hide the playlist bar` and `Hide the event badge`. Every rule that hides a kind of video stays, and so does `Hide inserted cards` (#48).
- `Swipe LIVEs in your Following row's order` is new with the other LIVE options in Playback. Open a LIVE from the row at the top of Following, and swiping up takes you through the row's other LIVEs in the order they sit there, starting with the next one and then going round to the ones before it. TikTok's own picks come after them, and the row's LIVEs don't show up a second time among those (#511).
- The Feature Gate Lab leaves TikTok's paid features alone. Gates tied to subscriptions, Super Fan, paid series, LIVE gifts, coins and the like aren't listed any more and can't be saved. A backup or shared profile holding one restores everything else, and a rule saved on one before this stays stored but does nothing.

Bug Fixes

- `Remove feed ads` now takes out the sponsored block some searches open with, the "Ad" banner for a brand with its videos and a Follow button. Searching "wildwood" showed one for a movie (#484).
- New patch, `Fix notifications on OPPO, OnePlus and realme`. On those phones TikTok also signs up for OPPO's push service, and OPPO only delivers to TikTok as TikTok signed it, so notifications sent that way can't reach a patched TikTok. TikTok now uses Google's push service there, the way it does on a Samsung or a Pixel. Other phones don't change. It's in the default selection, with no switch (#496).
- With `SIM spoof` on, pictures and thumbnails could stay grey unless a VPN was on. TikTok's network stack picked its image and API servers by the preset's country while the phone was on another country's network. The network stack now gets your real SIM's country and carrier, and the rest of TikTok still sees the preset (#415).
- With `Keep captions available` on, a video whose caption tracks don't include the one in its original language now shows one of the others. TikTok used to say the video had no captions even though it carried some. The export's Captions line counts those videos as `tracks:unmatched` (#217).
- `Show the country and date under the caption` no longer sits on the progress bar on videos without a search line under the caption. The line now goes right under the caption and keeps the gap TikTok leaves above the bar. It's white like the name and caption too, not the post time's grey (#498).
- `Hold TikTok's save button to download` works wherever you press on the save button. TikTok gives some accounts a check that only starts the long press when the press lands right on the icon or its count, and a hold beside them did nothing at all (#499).
- Record in a LIVE's small window used to do nothing when the room it belonged to had gone away in the meantime. Now it says "No stream found to record. Reopen the LIVE." and writes which part was missing to the log (#413).
- A translated caption at the top of the comments showed TikTok's raw tags around its hashtags and mentions, like `<h id="288">#flowers</h>`. It shows the plain text now, with the hashtags and mentions where TikTok draws them (#488).
- Tapping "more" on a translated caption at the top of the comments no longer switches it back to the original language. Captions with line breaks kept their original lines for the expanded view (#488).
- With the floating bottom bar, the top of the pill stuck up over the last row of Home's Community grid. On a page that ends at the bar, like that grid or the other tabs, the strip above the bar now matches the bottom area, so the pill sits inside it. Over videos it still stands a little above the bar (#436).
- A speed locked on one video and carried to the next ones by `Remember the last speed` now counts as locked there too, so pulling down on those videos lets the lock go. TikTok took them for 1x videos, so the pull just locked the same speed again and the bubble's padlock showed open (#485).
- With `Hide suggested accounts` on, following someone on a profile you opened from a video no longer leaves an empty "Suggested accounts" box under the buttons, and `Keep suggestions on profiles` now shows the suggestions there too. Both only worked on a profile opened on its own page (#462).
- With `Dark LIVE panels in dark mode` on, a pinned comment's Pinned and timer tags look the same in a LIVE you open from a search result as in any other room. That LIVE plays inside the search's video feed, which never got the room's light colors, so the tags sat on pale pills there (#362).
- `Hide Balance in the profile menu` no longer leaves a thin empty card where Balance was. Balance sits in a card of its own in that menu, and hiding its only row left the card's edges behind (#194).
- Photo saves from TikTok's own servers now send the sign-in TikTok's app sends there. Photos from a friend's story were refused without it, every copy, while TikTok showed them fine, and so were photos from private accounts you follow. No other site gets a cookie (#464, #504).
- Patching takes a lot less memory with most patches selected. All of them together now fit in a 1 GB patcher heap, where they used to run out at 1.5 GB. On a phone where Manager runs 32-bit, every patch now fits with TikTok's bundle and with the APK, where they ran out partway before. Several patches only look through TikTok's code, but every look made the patcher keep an editable copy of the method until the end. And each patch that changes TikTok's resources left the parsed resource table behind for the rest of the run, about 140 MB on the APK (#497, #460, #310, #441, #48).
- Stickers made from a video get the save box in chats now. Tapping one opens it after TikTok's own preview, and holding one shows Save media, which photo stickers, GIF stickers and AI stickers get in that menu too. TikTok handles all of those apart from its own stickers, so neither showed up for them (#470).
- With `Hide the music line` on, a video with a music line now has its caption the same distance above the progress bar as a video without one. The music line hid, but the space TikTok keeps under it stayed, so those captions sat a little higher (#512).
- `Keep captions in Clear display` shows a video's first caption when it's spoken now. 0.84.0 held on to that first caption for the kept line, but on the phone it looked for it in the wrong place and never found it, so the line stayed empty until TikTok sent the next caption, sometimes seconds later (#456).

The [changelog](https://github.com/SysAdminDoc/hushfeed/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md) has every earlier release too.

How to update

1. Update Morphe Manager to 2.7.0 or newer, then refresh the Hushfeed source.
2. Patch TikTok 47.9.3 from APKMirror. Keep the manager's existing signing key so your login and settings carry over.

The `.mpp` download is a patch bundle, not a TikTok APK. [Installation instructions](https://github.com/SysAdminDoc/hushfeed#install).

* Show update badge only when relevant patches are available ([#455](https://github.com/MorpheApp/morphe-desktop/issues/455)) ([4c9a3b8](https://github.com/MorpheApp/morphe-desktop/commit/4c9a3b8f972bf7ac22418258776b25e6f3146508))
* Stop root mount from keeping the old patched APK ([97be3df](https://github.com/MorpheApp/morphe-desktop/commit/97be3df70f3d90ea6304d09f6494024fbe58e419))
* Support fractional scaling on X11 and XWayland ([#446](https://github.com/MorpheApp/morphe-desktop/issues/446)) ([edfe717](https://github.com/MorpheApp/morphe-desktop/commit/edfe717d39456e26ffb6e2cd0a18fca2b2b73e8c))

* Update Patcher and ARSCLib dependency ([683899a](https://github.com/MorpheApp/morphe-desktop/commit/683899a9f2bcb531a3998de8ee3396dd6237f720))


### Features

* Add Codeberg and JSON patch source support ([b37c7b1](https://github.com/MorpheApp/morphe-desktop/commit/b37c7b1e3c8743147b51884b80eeca5236c7ec90))
* Add option to keep original APKs for repatching ([#445](https://github.com/MorpheApp/morphe-desktop/issues/445)) ([4c8659b](https://github.com/MorpheApp/morphe-desktop/commit/4c8659b25f9320993c4a405a20dda49399c76cc6))
* Install patched apps compiled with their baseline profile ([#459](https://github.com/MorpheApp/morphe-desktop/issues/459)) ([5950617](https://github.com/MorpheApp/morphe-desktop/commit/5950617dfff3f286821c068c9d9d416612291b42))


### Performance Improvements

* Speed up startup and loading of apps and patch options ([#454](https://github.com/MorpheApp/morphe-desktop/issues/454)) ([9683a7d](https://github.com/MorpheApp/morphe-desktop/commit/9683a7d82fb5b1c9dc010d2228f213bddf7b1481))

Bug Fixes

- `Remove feed ads` now takes out the sponsored block some searches open with, the "Ad" banner for a brand with its videos and a Follow button. Searching "wildwood" showed one for a movie (#484).
- New patch, `Fix notifications on OPPO, OnePlus and realme`. On those phones TikTok also signs up for OPPO's push service, and OPPO only delivers to TikTok as TikTok signed it, so notifications sent that way can't reach a patched TikTok. TikTok now uses Google's push service there, the way it does on a Samsung or a Pixel. Other phones don't change. It's in the default selection, with no switch (#496).
- With `SIM spoof` on, pictures and thumbnails could stay grey unless a VPN was on. TikTok's network stack picked its image and API servers by the preset's country while the phone was on another country's network. The network stack now gets your real SIM's country and carrier, and the rest of TikTok still sees the preset (#415).
- With `Keep captions available` on, a video whose caption tracks don't include the one in its original language now shows one of the others. TikTok used to say the video had no captions even though it carried some. The export's Captions line counts those videos as `tracks:unmatched` (#217).
- `Show the country and date under the caption` no longer sits on the progress bar on videos without a search line under the caption. The line now goes right under the caption and keeps the gap TikTok leaves above the bar. It's white like the name and caption too, not the post time's grey (#498).
- `Hold TikTok's save button to download` works wherever you press on the save button. TikTok gives some accounts a check that only starts the long press when the press lands right on the icon or its count, and a hold beside them did nothing at all (#499).
- Record in a LIVE's small window used to do nothing when the room it belonged to had gone away in the meantime. Now it says "No stream found to record. Reopen the LIVE." and writes which part was missing to the log (#413).
- A translated caption at the top of the comments showed TikTok's raw tags around its hashtags and mentions, like `<h id="288">#flowers</h>`. It shows the plain text now, with the hashtags and mentions where TikTok draws them (#488).
- Tapping "more" on a translated caption at the top of the comments no longer switches it back to the original language. Captions with line breaks kept their original lines for the expanded view (#488).
- With the floating bottom bar, the top of the pill stuck up over the last row of Home's Community grid. On a page that ends at the bar, like that grid or the other tabs, the strip above the bar now matches the bottom area, so the pill sits inside it. Over videos it still stands a little above the bar (#436).
- A speed locked on one video and carried to the next ones by `Remember the last speed` now counts as locked there too, so pulling down on those videos lets the lock go. TikTok took them for 1x videos, so the pull just locked the same speed again and the bubble's padlock showed open (#485).
- With `Hide suggested accounts` on, following someone on a profile you opened from a video no longer leaves an empty "Suggested accounts" box under the buttons, and `Keep suggestions on profiles` now shows the suggestions there too. Both only worked on a profile opened on its own page (#462).
- With `Dark LIVE panels in dark mode` on, a pinned comment's Pinned and timer tags look the same in a LIVE you open from a search result as in any other room. That LIVE plays inside the search's video feed, which never got the room's light colors, so the tags sat on pale pills there (#362).
- `Hide Balance in the profile menu` no longer leaves a thin empty card where Balance was. Balance sits in a card of its own in that menu, and hiding its only row left the card's edges behind (#194).
- Photo saves from TikTok's own servers now send the sign-in TikTok's app sends there. Photos from a friend's story were refused without it, every copy, while TikTok showed them fine, and so were photos from private accounts you follow. No other site gets a cookie (#464, #504).
- Patching takes a lot less memory with most patches selected. All of them together now fit in a 1 GB patcher heap, where they used to run out at 1.5 GB. On a phone where Manager runs 32-bit, every patch now fits with TikTok's bundle and with the APK, where they ran out partway before. Several patches only look through TikTok's code, but every look made the patcher keep an editable copy of the method until the end. And each patch that changes TikTok's resources left the parsed resource table behind for the rest of the run, about 140 MB on the APK (#497, #460, #310, #441, #48).
- Stickers made from a video get the save box in chats now. Tapping one opens it after TikTok's own preview, and holding one shows Save media, which photo stickers, GIF stickers and AI stickers get in that menu too. TikTok handles all of those apart from its own stickers, so neither showed up for them (#470).
- With `Hide the music line` on, a video with a music line now has its caption the same distance above the progress bar as a video without one. The music line hid, but the space TikTok keeps under it stayed, so those captions sat a little higher (#512).
- `Keep captions in Clear display` shows a video's first caption when it's spoken now. 0.84.0 held on to that first caption for the kept line, but on the phone it looked for it in the wrong place and never found it, so the line stayed empty until TikTok sent the next caption, sometimes seconds later (#456).

The [changelog](https://github.com/SysAdminDoc/hushfeed/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md) has every earlier release too.

How to update

1. Update Morphe Manager to 2.7.0 or newer, then refresh the Hushfeed source.
2. Patch TikTok 47.9.3 from APKMirror. Keep the manager's existing signing key so your login and settings carry over.

The `.mpp` download is a patch bundle, not a TikTok APK. [Installation instructions](https://github.com/SysAdminDoc/hushfeed#install).
